# Datus

> The trusted enterprise data context for AI agents.

Datus connects business ontology, semantic definitions, and data provenance in a shared data context layer. Teams can review business meaning; agents can use it in data engineering and analysis. The three pillars are Business-aware, Agent-native, and Audit-ready.

## Product relationships

- Datus Studio is the shared workspace for agent-driven data engineering and analysis. It brings files, SQL, results, and Agent conversations together.
- Datus Agent is an open-source data Agent for engineering and analysis. Semantic modeling is one capability alongside broader SQL and data workflows.
- DOSI is Datus's semantic execution runtime and can also be used independently. It validates compatible Apache Ossie definitions and compiles supported queries into native SQL for the selected supported data source.
- Apache Ossie (incubating) is the open, vendor-neutral specification. DOSI is a compatible runtime licensed under Elastic License 2.0; DOSI is not open-source. Datus Agent is open-source under Apache-2.0.

Ontology expresses business concepts and relationships connected to the semantic layer. Semantic definitions include metrics, dimensions, calculations, and source mappings. Reviewable definitions, generated SQL, and source references help teams inspect results; they do not automatically guarantee correctness. Reusing definitions across sources does not imply cross-warehouse federated execution or automatic learning from all feedback.

- [Datus](https://datus.ai/): Company positioning, product relationships, and capabilities.
- [Semantic Layer Solution](https://datus.ai/solutions/semantic-layer/): Shared business definitions, review workflows, and semantic execution for teams and agents.
- [Datus Studio](https://datus.ai/products/studio/): Team workspace for agent-driven data work.
- [Datus Agent](https://datus.ai/products/cli/): Open-source data engineering and analysis Agent.
- [DOSI](https://dosi.datus.ai/): Semantic execution runtime and supported interfaces.
- [Apache Ossie](https://ossie.apache.org/): The open specification project.
- [Datus documentation](https://docs.datus.ai/): Product documentation and configuration.

## Integration and modeling resources

- [Databases](https://datus.ai/databases/): Supported native database adapters and configuration.
- [Models](https://datus.ai/models/): Model-provider configuration.
- [Integrations](https://datus.ai/integrations/): Supported integrations and workflows.
- [Apache Ossie Converter](https://datus.ai/apache-ossie-converter/): Supported import and export paths, editable examples, and conversion diagnostics. Review compatibility before execution.
- [Cube to Apache Ossie](https://datus.ai/apache-ossie-converter/cube-to-ossie/): Import supported Cube YAML bundles with an editable three-file example.
- [Apache Ossie to dbt](https://datus.ai/apache-ossie-converter/ossie-to-dbt/): Export a MetricFlow semantic_manifest.json; this does not generate a runnable dbt project.
- [Apache Ossie to Snowflake](https://datus.ai/apache-ossie-converter/ossie-to-snowflake/): Generate Cortex Analyst YAML and review target diagnostics; reverse import is unavailable.
- [Apache Ossie Playground](https://datus.ai/tools/osi-playground/): Explore and validate supported semantic-model examples.
- [OSI Field Mapping](https://datus.ai/osi-field-mapping/): Compare semantic-model field mappings.
- [MCP](https://datus.ai/mcp/): Agent access through MCP.
- [Enterprise](https://datus.ai/products/enterprise/): Enterprise adoption and deployment information.
- [Pricing](https://datus.ai/pricing/): Current plans and commercial details.
